## Overview

In BaZi (Four Pillars of Destiny), the Day Master is the Heavenly Stem of your birth day — the "you" at the centre of the chart, around which everything else is read. Yours is Xin 辛 (Yin Metal): refined, precise, sensitive metal, like a jeweller's finish rather than a sword blade. You were born in the month of Shen 申 (Monkey), the first month of autumn, when metal is at its strongest in the year. That alone tilts the chart toward metal, and the numbers confirm it: metal makes up 45.9% of the chart, and the share of supporting elements (Friend, Rob Wealth and the Resource stars) is 51.2%. That puts you just over the line as a **strong Day Master** — self-sufficient, resilient, and able to carry weight, but also prone to hardening when life asks for flexibility.

The remaining elements are wood at 27.1%, water at 13.5%, fire at 8.2% and earth at a scarce 5.3%. Because the metal is already ample, the balancing elements — your favorable elements — are fire, water and wood. Fire gives Xin metal a purpose to warm and polish itself against; water keeps it flowing rather than rigid; wood gives it something meaningful to shape. Earth and metal are unfavorable because they add to what is already plentiful, which in daily life tends to show up as overthinking, over-preparing, or holding on too long.

The central theme of this chart is **refinement meeting pressure**. Your month pillar is Jia Shen 甲申, with Jia 甲 (Yang Wood) as Direct Wealth (steady, earned resources and tangible results) sitting on a branch whose main hidden stem, Geng 庚 (Yang Metal), is Rob Wealth (friendly competition and the pull of peers). Add the Nobleman star touching your year pillar and the Travelling Horse in your month, and the picture is of someone who does polished, careful work — and is repeatedly asked to do it in motion, among other ambitious people.

## Personality

Your day pillar is Xin Hai 辛亥, with the Day Master Xin over Hai 亥 (Pig). Hai's main hidden stem is Ren 壬 (Yang Water), which is your Hurting Officer — the expressive, quick-minded, slightly irreverent side that wants to say the clever thing and improve on the obvious one. This combination gives you a sharp inner voice: observant, articulate, with a taste for elegance and a low tolerance for sloppiness. Because you are a strong Day Master, that voice is confident rather than fragile, though it can tip into bluntness when you feel others are wasting time.

The year pillar, Geng Wu 庚午, puts Rob Wealth (peer energy, comparison, shared ambition) on the stem, over Wu 午 (Horse) whose main hidden stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is Seven Killings — pressure, challenge, and the drive it creates. Early environments or family patterns likely taught you to compete and to perform under scrutiny. The Nobleman star touching this pillar suggests support has often arrived through other people, even in competitive settings. The hour pillar, Xin Mao 辛卯, brings a Friend (a peer on your own wavelength) over Mao 卯 (Rabbit), whose main hidden stem Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) is Indirect Wealth (opportunity, side income, the unplanned gain) — and Mao also carries your Peach Blossom, the star of charm and attraction. The habit worth adjusting is the Xin tendency to polish endlessly before showing anything: with fire, water and wood as favorable, you are better served by putting imperfect work into the world and letting it be shaped by response.

## Career

The month pillar governs working life, and yours is Jia Shen 甲申 — Direct Wealth on the stem, the Ten God of steady salary, responsibility and measurable output, sitting over Rob Wealth in the hidden stems. That is a very clear signature: you are suited to roles where quality is judged and rewarded, and where you are surrounded by capable colleagues who keep you sharp. Because metal is strong, your standards are high and your work is meticulous; the risk is choosing environments so competitive that the joy drains out of the craft. Look for places where direct wealth accumulates — established organisations, specialist practices, anything with a visible product — rather than pure scramble.

The Travelling Horse touching your month pillar is one of your more telling features: movement is part of how you work well. Travel, cross-office projects, clients in other places, or a role that changes shape every year may suit you better than a static desk. The Hurting Officer hidden in your day branch (Ren 壬, Yang Water) is also a career asset — it handles communication, troubleshooting and the persuasive explanation of complex things. Putting that in front of people is more rewarding for you than keeping it internal.

The fire element is favorable and scarce (8.2%), and fire is what gives a strong metal chart direction. In practice this means visibility: taking the stage, presenting, being the named person on the work rather than the one behind it. Your Direct Wealth month stem wants results; your favorable fire wants those results seen.

## Wealth

Money in your chart has two distinct flavours. The first is Direct Wealth (Jia 甲, Yang Wood, your month stem): salary, contracts, retainers, the reliable number that arrives because you did the work. This is your natural mode and your strongest money channel — you are good at converting careful effort into something with a clear value. The second is Indirect Wealth (Yi 乙, Yin Wood, main hidden stem of your hour branch Mao 卯): the opportunistic, project-based, less predictable kind. Because it sits in the hour pillar — the part of the chart connected to later life and to what you build over time — this is the channel that tends to grow with you rather than replace the first.

The caution is Rob Wealth, which appears twice: as your year stem (Geng 庚, Yang Metal) and as the main hidden stem of your month branch (Geng again). Rob Wealth is the Ten God of shared resources and friendly competition, and when metal is already strong it can show up as money slipping toward other people, or as comparison-driven spending — buying to keep pace. Your earth and metal are unfavorable, so a practical habit is to make the direct-wealth side boringly solid and let any indirect-wealth experiments stay small and separate.

Keep the frame on habits rather than outcomes: track what actually comes in, set aside before you decide anything, and treat windfalls from the hour-pillar channel as extra rather than expected.

## Love and Relationships

The day branch is the seat of close relationships, and yours is Hai 亥 (Pig), whose main hidden stem Ren 壬 (Yang Water) is Hurting Officer. This is a warm, expressive, witty partner-signature: you communicate well and want someone who enjoys conversation and does not take your sharp observations personally. Hai is also your Void (Kong Wang) branch by the year pillar's reckoning — traditionally a note of slight detachment or idealism in that area, which in modern terms often simply means you need a partner who feels like a genuine intellectual equal rather than a comfortable default.

The Friendly side matters here. Your hour stem is Xin 辛, a Friend (peer energy on your own level), and the Peach Blossom touches that hour branch Mao — charm, attractiveness, and a social ease that tends to draw people in without effort. Meanwhile Seven Killings in your year branch (Ding 丁, Yin Fire) suggests you are drawn to people with drive and intensity, and that you handle pressure in relationships well as long as it is honest pressure rather than manipulation.

The habit worth softening: strong Xin metal plus Hurting Officer can express as a quick corrective remark where tenderness would land better. Because fire and water are favorable, the relationships that thrive for you are ones with warmth and flow — people who bring lightness and let you be less exacting. Give close connections room to be imperfect in the same way you are learning to allow in your work.

## Wellbeing Habits

With metal at 45.9%, the body-and-routine reading is about softening what is rigid. Sleep matters most: a strong Xin chart tends to run a busy mind late, and a consistent wind-down — dim light, no screens, a few minutes of slow breathing before bed — does more for you than any elaborate routine. Aim for regular hours rather than long ones; the aim is rhythm, not quantity.

Food-wise, the chart's scarcity of earth (5.3%) and the favorable pull toward water and wood suggest warm, cooked, grounding meals and plenty of hydration through the day. You may find you do better with meals at set times than with long gaps — the strong-metal tendency is to override hunger and keep working. Movement that involves flow rather than force suits you: walking, swimming, dancing, anything with a rhythm. Strength work is fine but keep it in proportion; the chart is already heavy on metal.

For emotional routines, the Hurting Officer in your day branch needs an outlet — writing, conversation, or a creative practice where you can be as precise as you like. And build in regular contact with people who make you laugh; the Friend and Peach Blossom in your hour pillar point to social lightness as genuine nourishment.

If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Current Luck Pillar

A Luck Pillar is a ten-year cycle, set by the direction of your birth, that colours the overall tone of a decade in the same way an annual pillar colours a single year. You are currently in your **Geng Chen 庚辰** Luck Pillar, which began in 2022 and runs to 2031 (ages 33 to 42). Its stem is Geng 庚 (Yang Metal), a Rob Wealth — peer competition, shared resources and comparison — and that stem is unfavorable in your chart, adding to a metal count that is already high. Its branch is Chen 辰 (Dragon), whose main hidden stem Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) is Direct Resource — learning, support, preparation, the slow building of foundations — and that branch is also unfavorable, because earth feeds metal.

Taken together, this is a decade of consolidating rather than expanding. The favorable fire, water and wood are relatively quiet in the Luck Pillar itself, so the rhythm of these years is steady, inward-facing and sometimes effortful: you may find yourself doing a lot of preparation, study, and quiet groundwork, with peers and competitors close at hand. That is not a bad thing — Direct Resource is the Ten God of genuine depth — but it rewards patience over visible wins.

The next Luck Pillar, **Ji Mao 己卯** (2032–2041, ages 43–52), shifts the emphasis noticeably. Its stem is Ji 己 (Yin Earth), an Indirect Resource — intuition, lateral learning — still unfavorable, but its branch Mao 卯 (Rabbit) carries Indirect Wealth and is favorable. That introduces the wood channel back into the foreground: opportunity, movement and a more outward, resourceful rhythm after a decade of building.

## Year by Year

Each Chinese solar year begins at Li Chun, the start of spring, and runs close to the calendar year. The years below are read in sequence against your current Luck Pillar.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

This is your Tai Sui year — the annual branch Wu 午 (Horse) matches your year-pillar branch, traditionally a year of more change and adjustment rather than anything ominous. The stem Bing 丙 (Yang Fire) is Direct Officer (authority, responsibility, structure and reputation) and the branch's main hidden stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is Seven Killings; both the stem and branch elements are favorable fire. Sitting inside your Geng Chen Luck Pillar, this is one of the brighter years of the decade for stepping into responsibility and being recognised for it. Relations are active: your year pillar self-punishes with Wu, and the 2026 stem combines with both your day stem and your hour stem — a year of realignment in how you present yourself and how you relate to others.

Lean into visible responsibility. This is a good time to take on a named role or a public-facing piece of work, and to let your Direct Officer side be seen. In the first half of the year, be a little more deliberate about routines and agreements, since the self-punishment and stem combinations suggest shifting arrangements. Toward the end of the year, the pace tends to settle.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is Seven Killings — pressure, challenge and the drive it creates — favorable, while the branch Wei 未 (Goat) is earth and unfavorable. The year branch combines with your year branch and forms a triad with your day and hour branches, so relationships and collaborations are unusually lively; the Wei branch's main hidden stem is Indirect Resource, which supports learning and inner replenishment. The overall tone is energetic, driven, and socially expanding.

This is a good year to say yes to a challenge that stretches you, and to lean on the people your chart keeps bringing close. In the second half of the year, watch for overcommitment — Seven Killings plus a triad of connections can mean a full plate.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The stem Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) is Direct Resource (learning and support) and unfavorable, and the branch Shen 申 (Monkey) is metal, also unfavorable. Neither is a difficult year, but it sits inside the Geng Chen decade's already-heavy earth-and-metal tone — a year for consolidation rather than launch. The one notable relation is a triad with your Luck Pillar, which suggests steady progress on long-term groundwork.

This is a good year to put time into training, qualifications, or a project that needs patience. Keep your calendar realistic, and enjoy the quiet.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The stem Ji 己 (Yin Earth) is Indirect Resource and the branch You 酉 (Rooster) is metal, both unfavorable, so this is a year for maintenance. The relations are busy: the stem combines with your month stem, the branch clashes with your hour branch, and it forms a six harmony with your Luck Pillar. In plain terms, working arrangements may shift and close relationships may feel more changeable — and the clash with your hour branch touches the area of your chart that carries the Peach Blossom.

Slow down and talk things through, particularly where work and dear ones overlap. This is a good year to review commitments rather than add to them.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The stem Geng 庚 (Yang Metal) is Rob Wealth and the branch Xu 戌 (Dog) is earth — both unfavorable — which makes this the most "metal-heavy" year of the window. Relations are significant: the year branch forms a triad with your year pillar, a six harmony with your hour branch, and a clash with your Luck Pillar. That clash suggests the rhythm of the decade shifts noticeably. Notably, the year branch also corresponds to one of the Void branches attached to your day pillar, which is a soft signal to be extra deliberate about what you take on.

Lean into partnership rather than solo effort, and keep your expectations of yourself flexible. This is a year where moving with change serves better than resisting it.

## Guidance

- **Make your work visible.** Fire is favorable and only 8.2% of the chart, so presenting, publishing and being the named person on a project feeds a genuine need — the Direct Officer energy of 2026 is the natural moment to start.
- **Keep the metal from hardening.** With metal at 45.9% and Rob Wealth appearing in both your year stem and month branch, build in deliberate breaks from comparison — a weekly review of what you have done rather than what others have.
- **Use the Travelling Horse in your month pillar.** Movement is a working style, not a distraction: choose a project or role that involves travel or change of scene in the next year or two.
- **Let the Hurting Officer speak.** Ren 壬 (Yang Water) in your day branch is favorable; give it a regular outlet in writing or conversation, especially in 2027 when Seven Killings brings pressure that needs expressing rather than holding.
- **Prepare patiently through the Geng Chen years.** With the current Luck Pillar's earth and metal both unfavorable, spend the mid-2020s on depth and qualification; the wood channel of the Ji Mao Luck Pillar that begins in 2032 shifts the emphasis outward.
